text.p: Ameritech Corp said the double-digit growth it reported for its 1996 fourth quarter is sustainable, as the company continues to expand without wandering far from its core telephone service business.

Ameritech, a regional Bell operating company, reported on Monday fourth quarter earnings of $552 million, a 10.2 percent increase from $501 million reported in 1995, both before one-time items. Revenues climbed 10 percent to $3.9 billion from $3.5 billion.
"We believe they (growth rates) are sustainable," Oren Schaffer, Ameritech chief financial officer, said in an interview.
"In fact, our objective going forward is to continue the sustainability of double-digit growth," he said.

The company said the fourth quarter was the 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit profit growth and the fifth of double-digit revenue increases. The company's $1.00 fourth quarter earnings per share before one-time items was just above the consensus of analysts' estimates of $0.99.

Ameritech became the first regional company to file for permission to provide long-distance telephone service in its area. It filed in Michigan, and Schaffer said the company plans to file in other states during the first quarter.
Schaffer said Ameritech has already set up its long-distance business, including operations, networks and advertising, declining to specify costs.
"We paid for those in 1996 and still sustained our double-digit growth," Schaffer said.
Analysts pointed out, however, that Ameritech's telephone line growth slowed. It fell to 3.4 percent in the fourth quarter from 3.7 in the third, which was also a decline.
"In Ameritech, you are seeing a continuation of slower line growth," said Richard Klugman, analyst at PaineWebber. He noted that Ameritech was turning its attention elsewhere.
In fact, Ameritech said added services such as call waiting and caller I.D. have more growth potential, considering most people in the region have phone lines but few have voice mail, for example.
Ameritech said call management services, as they are called, grew 23.5 percent over 1995, the highest rate ever.

Security monitoring is also one of Ameritech's promising businesses, Schaffer said. The company said it expanded its North American business to 367,000 customers, making it the largest provider in Canada and second largest in the $13 billion U.S. market.

"Security monitoring is clearly one of the growth industries of the future," Schaffer said, adding it has a very low penetration rate at the residential level. "It's based on the public's need for peace of mind."
In addition, it is another added service to make Ameritech a one-stop shop.

"It binds your customer base to Ameritech," said Robert Wilkes, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman. He noted that becomes even more important when competition takes hold in the local telephone market. "You can get one bill."
